packageRules.description: fastmcp carries the MCP protocol layer under both servers (protocol era negotiation, elicitation wire mechanism, list-cache hints), so a bump always gets human review instead of automerging.

The custom manager below rewrites only the omnigraph VERSION lines. It leaves the release tag and asset digests on the old release, so CI tests the old binary under the new label (agent-kit#342). A release can also move the storage format, which means rebuilding every deployed graph (0.11.0 moved it from 6 to 9). A bump always needs a human to move the tag, digests and _OMNIGRAPH_INTERNAL_SCHEMA, and to plan any rebuild.

customManagers.description: The omnigraph binary version, pinned in THREE places that must move together: witan-core's shared installer (what `witan setup` fetches onto a developer's PATH), and the two Dockerfiles (what the deployed data tier and the MCP tier's bundled CLI run). A partial bump ships a client and a server on different releases, and omnigraph uses strict single-version storage — a 0.8.x binary refuses a 0.9.x graph and vice versa — so a split-version deploy is a hard outage, not a soft degradation. `just check-omnigraph-pins` enforces agreement in CI as a backstop.
